Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Nexa CTO), Raj (Nexa ML), Emily (Nexa DevOps)

Summary: Quick POC check-in. Reviewed onboarding progress (VPC access, service accounts), initial perf regressions on long-context recency, discussed quantization tradeoffs and next steps for benchmarks and security docs.

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time. Quick roll call?
00:12 - Sofia: Hi, Sofia here. Raj and Emily on—we're good.
00:16 - Raj: Morning.
00:20 - Liam: Liam here from Redwood, I'll be running the perf tests and looking at model tuning.
00:26 - Maya: Cool. Agenda is quick status on access & infra, quick review of early results we shared, then plan next steps.
00:34 - Speaker 1: Sounds good.

00:45 - Maya: Emily, wanted to start with you—where are we on the VPC peering and the egress IPs needed for the POC?
00:52 - Emily: Yeah so we created the service account and started the firewall rules, I ran into one blocker with our security team around static egress. basically they want a confirmed list of IPs for allowlisting, and we need the peering to be approved.
01:06 - Maya: Understood. We'll send the egress list and peering instructions today. Liam, you have the IP list?
01:12 - Liam: Yep, I'll attach the full list and the small network diagram. Note there are two sets: hosted endpoints and dedicated pool ranges depending on whether they pick Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated later.
01:30 - Emily: Got it, that helps. If we go dedicated we'd need additional approvals but for the pilot hosted is fine.

01:40 - Raj: Quick question on data handling — if we send sample logs to test recency, do you persist them? We need confirmation they won't be used to train models.
01:50 - Maya: Yes, for Hosted POC we have a no-training policy for customer payloads; we'll include that language in the security docs. We also have KMS options if you want encrypted at rest.
02:02 - Sofia: Great. Please make sure the SOC2 statements are explicit.

02:15 - Liam: On the perf side, we ran the first pass of 500 prompts through the redwood:r4-open model variant with prefix caching enabled. Results: average p95 latency is about 420ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) but jumps to ~1.2s for 4k context with KV warm, and we saw a couple cold-cache spikes to 2.8s.
02:40 - Raj: Those cold spikes are concerning—our user SLAs expect sub-1s for most synchronous interactions.
02:46 - Liam: Yep, understood. Two quick levers: increase batching threshold and enable quantized model profile (we tested int8-like path) — that drops p95 by roughly 20-30% but can change token-level quality slightly for rare tokens.
03:02 - Raj: What's the tradeoff for hallucination/quality? We can't accept regressions on clinical-sounding outputs.
03:08 - Liam: For general QA we saw small drift on rare medical entities in int8-like runs; for your use case, we recommend a hybrid: use fp16 for long-form clinical recency and int8 for common user prompts, or run post-generation verification with your classifier. Also we can run an eval set you provide.
03:28 - Sofia: We'd like an eval focused on med terms and entity fidelity — Raj will compile a short test set.
03:36 - Raj: Yep I'll have a 200-example eval by Monday (2026-05-17).

03:45 - Speaker 2: (mumble)
03:48 - Maya: Ok, that's helpful. On onboarding status, I see in our tracker that service account is created, but the VPC peering is still pending. Emily, any ETA on approvals?
03:56 - Emily: Security asked for the network diagram and SOC2 evidence; once they review we'll have peering done—hoping by Tuesday this coming week.
04:06 - Maya: We'll get both docs to you today.

04:12 - Raj: Another perf note, when you say KV warm, what's the warm window? We've seen cache evictions in our workload due to many distinct user sessions.
04:22 - Liam: The default TTL on prefix cache is 30 minutes but it depends on memory and cluster sizing. For high session churn we can pin keys for high-value conversations or increase cache allocation; both increase RAM utilization on the GPU nodes.
04:34 - Raj: So that means more cost. Can you quantify?
04:37 - Liam: Rough back-of-envelope: doubling cache allocation for your 2x workload footprint increases instance RAM needs ~40% and roughly 15-20% on cost per token, but p95 latency improves substantially and cold spike frequency drops. We'll quantify in the benchmark.
04:52 - Sofia: We need a clear cost vs latency table to present to finance.
04:56 - Maya: We'll include that. Liam will run configs A/B during the benchmark.

05:05 - Maya: Any blockers on identity/auth? SSO SAML config?
05:09 - Emily: We started SSO but need the assertion consumer URL; can you confirm?
05:12 - Maya: Yes, sending the ACS and metadata today.

05:20 - Liam: Quick note on routing: in case you later use Dedicated we can route by policy so latency-sensitive traffic hits the dedicated pool while less sensitive hits hosted cheaper variants — helps manage cost.
05:34 - Raj: If we go dedicated, how disruptive is the migration? Data residency/legal wise we might prefer dedicated.
05:40 - Maya: Migration is mostly config-level, pinning model versions and updating endpoints. We do a canary rollout and fallback so it should be low risk. We'll capture the migration plan in the runbook.

05:52 - Speaker 3: um
05:55 - Emily: One more on observability—what do you expose? We need traces token-level cost breakdown and request logs for audits.
06:02 - Liam: We expose per-route latency histograms, token-level cost estimates, and request/response logging with redaction options. For audits we can provide retained audit logs as an add-on.
06:14 - Sofia: Ok include retention options and price.

06:20 - Maya: Let's recap: action items—Liam to run expanded perf tests (cold/warm, int8/fp16, batch sizes) and share CSV + summary by 2026-05-21. Raj to provide eval set by 2026-05-17. Emily to open peering request and provide subnet details by 2026-05-18. Maya to send SOC2 summary, network diagram, and ACS URL today (2026-05-14).
06:45 - Raj: Sounds good. Also, can you include the exact IP ranges for both Hosted and Dedicated in the network doc?
06:52 - Liam: Yep will include both.
06:56 - Sofia: Last Q—competitors. We've been asked if you integrate with Anthropic endpoints or Bedrock; what's your position?
07:05 - Maya: We can integrate downstream models but the POC is focused on Redwood runtime to evaluate latency/cost. We'll note options in the vendor comparison doc.
07:14 - Raj: Cool.
07:18 - Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll share the packet tonight and follow up with the benchmark. Next sync same time next week?
07:26 - Sofia: Works for us.
07:28 - Emily: Good.
07:30 - Maya: Great, meeting adjourned.
